event_text: An unrelated AT&T outage (app and network) ended before the window
Newark airport weather radar out
Milwaukee airport weather radar out until 3:53 PM
O'Hare ground stop: "EQUIPMENT/OUTAGE, COMMS ISSUES"
Midway ground stop
O'Hare arrivals told to expect airborne holding for equipment issues
Moline Ground holds SkyWest 4792: "Chicago approach is going ATC zero"
Chicago controller: "We lost all the frequencies and all the automation for the handoff and strips"
Boston approach frequency problem
Diversion-recovery tool turned on for all airports
Kansas City Center reportedly the starting point
Potomac approach and Washington Center restrictions
Washington Center stops all departures; IFR Meter's own feeds go silent for about 3 minutes
Boston weather office: "Boston Center reported teleco issues actively being worked"
NBAA notice: "frequency and radar outages at several ARTCCs"
National ground stop for all US airports
Seattle Ground to SkyWest 4179: "All en route facilities are having communication issues… it started with Chicago"
Chicago Center (ZAU) cites an equipment outage; drop times extended
FAA Advisory 117 calls it a "nationwide comms failure"
Bloomberg, citing one unnamed person: the FBI is looking at whether a software update caused the outage and does not believe it was a cyberattack or crime
O'Hare route stops cancelled, but delays reach 136–150 minutes
Domestic stop still on. International and oceanic departures released from New York, Philadelphia and the San Francisco Bay Area. Toronto and Montreal stop flights to the US.
More than 10,000 delays and 1,200 cancellations; cancellations nearly tripled in 30 minutes
Cleveland Center traffic arriving at Newark via PENNS stopped until midnight, citing FAA equipment
Advisory 120 reissues the stop until 11 PM with reason "COMMUNICATIONS FAILURE". Advisory 119 sets a tiered release as en route centers recover.
No departures resuming in the data yet; about 646 flights in arrival metering versus about 3,170 at the same time yesterday
Potomac departures over SWANN converted from a stop to spaced departures until 9 PM; possibly a first small release step
FAA: every flight accounted for; international flights handled case by case
Delta, American and United: no new departures, flights in the air continue; Delta and American waive change fees
Some flights to Asia, Hawaii, Alaska and Europe departed; later corroborated as coastal international releases
Reagan National at capacity, O'Hare nearing capacity; Newark controllers "running out of space"
1,913 cancellations and 10,494 delays
Advisories 121 and 122 are unrelated (Starship reroute cancelled; Guatemala volcanic ash)
Mullin: Trump briefed; officials "not ruling out anything," cyberattack "not known"
O'Hare departure delays 181–195 minutes; Houston Intercontinental 165 minutes; Fort Lauderdale closed to diversions until 4 AM
Still no domestic restart; 471 flights in arrival metering versus 2,987 yesterday. Stop stays through 11 PM under Advisory 120.
CBS, citing multiple sources: an update to the private ATC communications network caused a reboot and crash; the system is operated by L3Harris
Advisory 123 is unrelated (Sangay, Ecuador volcanic ash bulletin)
Hawaii DOT halted all Hawaii–West Coast flights, citing SpaceX launch debris; the halt appears precautionary and is unrelated to the FAA outage
At least 827 flights diverted
Reagan National closed to diversion aircraft until 6 AM ET
Advisory 001 changes the stop to a nationwide ground stop with selective releases; some coastal facilities released international departures
Advisory 002 suspends a routing program at Washington Center over erroneous route filings; not a recovery step
Fort Lauderdale closure to diversions reissued for capacity, until 4 AM ET
American Airlines: some flights from certain airports are getting clearance to depart; most departures still paused
No restart after the 7:15 PM planning call; national stop still listed until 11 PM ET; next FAA planning webinar 9:15 PM ET
O'Hare departure delays reach 5 hours, reason FAA equipment
The nationwide ground stop is cancelled for all airports and all facilities
Ground-delay programs cancelled at LaGuardia, Boston, Las Vegas, San Diego and San Francisco

Release times are being issued again; the FAA status summary no longer lists the national stop. Arrival metering is 136 flights versus 2,921 yesterday. The Newark PENNS restriction is still listed until midnight.

About 9,124 US delays remain; O'Hare about 5 hours (equipment) and Atlanta about 3 hours. United, JetBlue and Air Canada cancel most remaining Friday flights; nearly 5,000 Friday cancellations and about 800 Saturday.
Mullin and Duffy brief reporters in the White House Brady Briefing Room after the lift: Mullin says "no cyberattack" and the public was never in danger
New O'Hare ground stop (second tier, reason "other"), Advisory 011, listed until 9:45 PM ET
Duffy: airspace opened at 8:15 PM ET; centers and TRACONs operational; recovery will take time
Duffy describes radar and communications "instability," says they did not lose all telecom or radar, and gives aircraft counts
FAA relabels the O'Hare stop: United and its subsidiaries only, at the airline's request
Carrier-only ground stops at Seattle, San Diego, Newark and Minneapolis
FAA closes its TCA/hotline web pages
Newark PENNS stop no longer listed
FAA overnight operations plan
Newark United stop cancelled; O'Hare extended; Los Angeles Alaska stop
Airline-requested stops extended at San Diego, Seattle and Minneapolis
O'Hare United-only stop narrowed to first tier plus Canada, still until 10:45 PM ET
United's O'Hare stop and Alaska's Seattle stop cancelled; Alaska's San Diego stop extended to 11 PM ET
New American-only stop at Dallas–Fort Worth until 12:30 AM ET; Alaska's Los Angeles stop extended to midnight ET
San Diego and Minneapolis stops cancelled; new American-only stop at O'Hare until 1:30 AM ET
New Delta-only stop at Atlanta until 1 AM ET; FAA lists American's O'Hare stop as an airline request
Alaska's Los Angeles stop cancelled; FAA lists Delta's Atlanta stop as an airline request
Delta's Atlanta stop cancelled
American's Dallas–Fort Worth stop cancelled
American's O'Hare stop cancelled; no ground stops listed
Officials name a cause: overloaded legacy TDM switches and routers; new equipment overwhelmed the old system
FAA morning operations plan lists only routine constraints
Friday ends with about 9,132 US cancellations; about 3,374 more by Saturday morning
FAA cancels the outage-era extended flight plan drop times
About 3,502 US cancellations so far Saturday
Duffy says it is safe to fly and announces a 10:30 AM ET briefing with Bedford
Duffy/Bedford DOT briefing: Duffy names L3Harris copper-to-fiber work at a remote site
More than 4,000 US cancellations Saturday
2009 precedent: Harris Corp. router misconfiguration during fiber move
More than 4,700 cancellations; FAA back at full operations
L3Harris statement: supporting the FAA investigation
DOT posts written briefing remarks: over 1,000 connection attempts every 4–5 seconds
Routers in Arkansas and Texas may have had problems; 17 of 22 en route centers affected
Bedford: FAA routinely replacing about 2,000 Cisco 600 routers with Juniper routers
PASS union: issue isolated to two contractor routers "being updated mid-day"
POLITICO: internal FAA memo cites "data saturation"
WSJ: Juniper routers at El Dorado, Ark., and Amarillo, Texas; trouble first seen at Indianapolis Center
Saturday cancellations top 6,000
House T&I Democrats: staff briefing Monday; Bedford expected at an early December hearing
FAA written Q&A names the two sites: El Dorado, Ark., radio site and Amarillo, Texas, radar site
Duffy on Sunday shows: routers in L3Harris lab in Florida; FBI offered help; no sign of a foreign cyberattack
DOT written release: Duffy says the routers that had trouble were bought in 2001 and obsolete by 2006
Duffy on ABC: broadcast turned off on 69 routers; the Amarillo router, replaced about 3 weeks earlier, began flooding when the El Dorado router came on
Router maker HPE: the device "functioned as it was configured to by the installer. It did not fail or act improperly"
Lab tests: FAA, Juniper and Cisco engineers assisting L3Harris diagnostics in Florida; FBI involved
Fri–Sun cancellations about 18,100 (FlightAware)
Records: 2024 DOT IG audit found 10 improperly authorized FTI contract extensions
Funding fight: $10.1 billion of the $30.1 billion request is for ATC; government funding runs out Dec. 11
Operations near normal: no ground stops; only weather/volume delay programs
Hearing check: no new House T&I hearing posted; the BNATCS hearing set for Nov. 10 is still "postponed until further notice"
Funding ask grows to up to $50 billion; Democrats say $9 billion of $14.4 billion already appropriated is unspent
Debunked: viral claim that Trump and top aides were moved to a secure bunker during the outage
Rumor: "Israel hacked US airspace" posts on X; no evidence
Duffy on CNBC: still unclear why the El Dorado router flooded the network; outage cost "billions"; FBI agents at the L3Harris lab
Hill briefings: House T&I staff briefing reported moved to Tuesday; Duffy expected at the Senate GOP lunch Tuesday
Senate Commerce Democrats urge the FAA to pause further Juniper router installs pending testing
FBI: Cyber teams giving technical assistance; FBI "has not taken possession of any equipment"
Administration formally requests $50.1 billion; $10.1 billion for ATC technology including more resilient telecom
Duffy and Bedford pitch the $50 billion at the Senate GOP lunch; Republicans skeptical
DOT: investigators recreated the El Dorado overload in the lab; root cause still unclear
Washington Post: an FAA official supervised, tested and signed off on the El Dorado work minutes before the network faltered
KATV: internal FAA documents show reduced FAA review of contractor work at telecom sites
CRN source: the El Dorado device is a copper-to-fiber converter with a multicast feature
White House release: the Director of National Intelligence says the recent outages are "not a cyberattack"
Bedford says investigators are "very close" to the root cause and an announcement is expected this week
White House cyber director Sean Cairncross out; Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies named
Duffy says the ground stop could have ended sooner if the network contractor had found the problem faster
Bedford says the contractor's engineer was monitored by an FAA technician during the El Dorado installation
Bedford says the FAA thought the router function was disabled and does not yet know how the configuration changed
Trump calls the recent outages separate events and blames the ground stop on aging FAA equipment
Bedford says the FAA spent about 45 minutes unable to find the cause, partly because maintenance is logged on paper
Trump confirms he fired cyber director Sean Cairncross, saying he wasn't "good enough"
the Director of National Intelligence tells ABC that this week's outages, including the FAA's, were not coordinated and not state-sponsored
the Director of National Intelligence tells CNN that more interruptions are possible as systems are upgraded
the White House interagency tiger team on preventing another ground stop holds its first meeting, CBS reports
